title: Large Spiral Plate Heat Exchanger Delivered for Mining Service
excerpt: Nexson Group has reported delivery of a very large liquid-liquid spiral plate heat exchanger for mineral slurry cooling and solvent heating service.
author: HeatEx Direct Editorial Team
reviewer: HeatEx Direct Editorial Team
content:
Nexson Group has reported the delivery of an unusually large Type 1 liquid-liquid spiral plate heat exchanger for a mining process application. The equipment is described as nearly 4 meters in diameter and close to 30 tons in weight, with more than 800 m2 of heat transfer area and duplex stainless steel construction.

The reported duty is a combined process step: cooling mineral slurry while heating a solvent stream. That pairing is a natural use case for spiral plate heat exchangers because the design can support efficient liquid-liquid heat recovery while keeping a relatively compact footprint.

Why This Delivery Matters

Spiral plate heat exchangers occupy a specialized position in the heat exchanger market. Their basic structure is simple to describe: two metal sheets are wound into spiral channels, creating two separated flow paths with heat transfer through the plate wall. In practice, making that geometry reliable at large diameter, high area, and industrial pressure is a demanding manufacturing task.

Large mining and hydrometallurgy projects often involve abrasive slurry, suspended solids, and process liquids that can foul conventional equipment. A spiral channel can help because it creates continuous curvature, strong secondary flow, and a single-flow-path behavior that reduces stagnant zones.

Application Signal

The delivery points to three broader trends in industrial heat transfer:

  • Slurry services are moving toward more compact heat recovery equipment when cleaning access and fouling resistance can be engineered properly.
  • Duplex stainless steel remains a practical material choice for duties where corrosion resistance and mechanical strength are both important.
  • Large spiral plate units are increasingly considered for mineral processing and energy-intensive industrial operations, not only for smaller utility duties.

Buyer Takeaway

For buyers evaluating spiral plate technology, headline size is only one part of the story. The more important questions are flow distribution, solids tolerance, pressure drop, cleaning method, weld quality, inspection documentation, and the supplier's ability to prove performance in similar slurry service.

This reported delivery is therefore less about a single record-sized unit and more about the continuing expansion of spiral plate heat exchangers into difficult liquid-liquid process applications.

title: 大型螺旋板式换热器交付矿业浆液工况
excerpt: Nexson Group 披露交付一台大型液-液螺旋板式换热器，用于矿物浆液冷却与溶剂加热的组合工况。
author: HeatEx Direct 编辑团队
reviewer: HeatEx Direct 编辑团队
content:
Nexson Group 近期披露，其交付了一台用于矿业流程的大型 1 型液-液螺旋板式换热器。公开信息显示，该设备直径接近 4 米，重量接近 30 吨，换热面积超过 800 m2，并采用双相不锈钢材料。

该设备对应的是一个组合换热任务：一侧冷却矿物浆液，另一侧加热溶剂流。对这类液-液热回收场景而言，螺旋板式结构有天然适配性，因为它能够在相对紧凑的空间内实现较高传热强度，并尽量减少低流速死区。

为什么这次交付值得关注

螺旋板式换热器在换热器市场中属于有门槛的专用设备。它的基本结构不难理解：两张金属板被卷制成螺旋通道，形成两条彼此隔离的流体路径，冷热介质通过板壁完成换热。但要把这种结构做到大直径、大面积、工业压力等级，并保持长期可靠性，制造难度并不低。

矿业和湿法冶金项目经常面对磨蚀性浆液、悬浮固体和容易结垢的工艺液。螺旋通道的连续曲率、二次流和单通道流动特征，可以降低局部滞流和沉积风险。

应用信号

这次交付释放出几个行业信号：

  • 当清洗通道和抗结垢设计处理得当时，浆液工况也在考虑更紧凑的热回收设备。
  • 对同时需要耐腐蚀和结构强度的场景，双相不锈钢仍然是重要材料选择。
  • 大型螺旋板设备正在从常规公用工程应用，进入矿物加工和高能耗工业流程中的关键换热环节。

采购方应关注什么

对采购方而言，设备尺寸只是表层信息。真正需要审查的是流体分布、固体通过能力、压降、清洗方式、焊接质量、检验文件，以及供应商在类似浆液工况中的项目经验。

因此，这次交付的意义不只是单台设备很大，而是说明螺旋板式换热器正在继续向复杂液-液过程换热场景拓展。

author: Shanghai Accessen Co., Ltd.
reviewer: Shanghai Accessen Co., Ltd.
content:
The 13th China Data Center Standards Summit (CDCC SUMMIT 2025) grandly opened at the Beijing National Convention Center under the theme "Redefining the AI Foundation." Shanghai Accessen, as a provider of data center cooling system solutions, participated in the exhibition showcasing its data center products and low-carbon heat exchange solutions. These included prefabricated integrated cooling stations, liquid cooling hydraulic modules, coolant distribution units (CDUs), and new liquid cooling products (Manifold). Data center cooling systems, being fundamental to safe operation, were a key focus among the attending experts.

In this era of explosive growth in AI computing power, where traditional IDCs are rapidly transitioning to AIDCs, the heat dissipation capacity required for higher cabinet power densities has made cooling systems a core infrastructure element in data centers. Accessen is redefining data center thermal management paths through liquid cooling technology. By integrating prefabrication and intelligent features, it addresses the pain points of cooling efficiency and energy consumption control in high-density computing scenarios. Its philosophy of "standardized design + modular expansion" aligns closely with the industry's low-carbon transformation goals, driving the development of data centers towards greater specialization, integration, convergence, sustainability, collaboration, and security.

Leveraging nearly two decades of product technology and application experience in the heat exchange field, Accessen's prefabricated, low-carbon data center heat exchange solutions offer a product series encompassing both water-cooling and liquid-cooling. The core portfolio includes prefabricated integrated cooling stations, AHRI-certified high-efficiency plate heat exchangers, liquid cooling hydraulic modules, and coolant distribution units. These solutions deeply articulate the technical advantages in terms of energy efficiency improvement, rapid deployment, safe operation and maintenance, and green sustainability, empowering data center clients to break from convention, foster continuous innovation, and achieve sustainable data center development.

Achieving rapid, high-quality delivery of efficient data centers has become a core competitive differentiator recognized by the industry. Accessen's leading prefabricated integrated cooling station solutions cover both indoor and outdoor application scenarios. The AIS prefabricated integrated cooling station is a product that structurally optimizes and highly integrates key components of the refrigeration system (including chillers, plate heat exchangers, pumps, cooling towers, valves, intelligent control systems, and auxiliary components). By integrating high-efficiency plate heat exchangers and intelligent control systems, and adopting a factory pre-installed, pre-commissioned model, it operates immediately upon connection to water and power on-site. This reduces project deployment cycles by 50% compared to traditional installation methods. Optimized internal piping and design within the station lower energy consumption by over 20%, meeting the rapid expansion needs of both new and retrofit data center projects.

Accessen's ACDU series coolant distribution units incorporate modular design and standardized architecture, significantly reducing data center cooling energy consumption and enabling breakthrough optimization of PUE. They support the heat dissipation demands of high-density AI computing deployments, enabling precise and intelligent allocation of cooling capacity to meet the surging cooling needs of AI data centers. Customized liquid cooling system solutions are also available based on client requirements.

Continuously iterating and upgrading its prefabricated products and solutions, Accessen provides clients with green, low-carbon support characterized by "rapid deployment, energy efficiency optimization, and intelligent regulation." Its solutions have been successfully applied in dozens of projects, including those for China Mobile, China Unicom, Gangcheng Yunlian, GLP Changshu, BDC and GDS. With representative offices established in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Hong Kong, and other locations, Accessen provides support for data center projects in Southeast Asia and has successfully implemented multiple overseas projects in countries like the Philippines, Thailand, and Malaysia.

The summit also announced a rigorously selected list of 10 outstanding project cases and 17 advanced application technologies. These stand as shining beacons, guiding the development of the data center industry and serving as a "value compass" within the field.

The "2025 Top 10 Outstanding Data Center Projects" award serves as a benchmark demonstration window for data center full-lifecycle practices. It focuses on the safety, reliability, green energy efficiency, and sustainable development capabilities of implemented projects, providing the industry with replicable construction and operation models.

title: Accessen to Showcase Prefabricated Cooling Solutions at DCWF 2026
excerpt: Accessen announced that it would exhibit prefabricated integrated cooling station solutions at Data Centre World Frankfurt 2026.
author: Shanghai Accessen Co., Ltd.
reviewer: Shanghai Accessen Co., Ltd.
content:
Accessen, a leading provider of prefabricated integrated cooling station solutions for data centers, is pleased to announce its participation in Data Centre World Frankfurt 2026 (DCWF), taking place from May 6-7, 2026, at Messe Frankfurt, Hall 8, Germany. Accessen will be exhibiting at Booth M155, where the company will present its latest innovations in modular, prefabricated thermal management solutions designed for next-generation data centers.

As part of Tech Show Frankfurt--the most important technology event in the DACH region--Data Centre World Frankfurt 2026 is expected to attract nearly 400 global exhibitors and over 12,000 industry professionals. The event brings together the region's data center community for two days of innovation, insight, and networking. With its 2026 conference programme focusing on "Net Zero Data Centres: AI-Ready, Carbon-Smart, Always-On," the event provides an ideal platform for Accessen to demonstrate how its prefabricated cooling solutions address the industry's most pressing challenges--balancing performance with sustainability.

Meeting Europe's Growing Demand for Rapid, Sustainable Deployment

The European modular data center market is projected to reach USD 18.60 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 14.6%, driven by stringent EU energy-efficiency regulations and accelerating demand for faster deployment models. Within this landscape, Germany stands as a key market, with the country's data center cooling sector expected to grow from USD 1.15 billion in 2025 to USD 7.16 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of 20.4%. This rapid growth underscores the urgent need for scalable, energy-efficient cooling solutions that can keep pace with AI-driven infrastructure demands.

Accessen is uniquely positioned to meet this demand. With nearly two decades of expertise in heat exchange technology, the company has successfully delivered over 20,000 customized thermal management solutions worldwide, earning the trust of industry leaders including China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom, ByteDance, Huawei, Tencent, and GLP. Its prefabricated cooling solutions have been deployed across dozens of major data center projects, providing reliable thermal management for hyperscale, colocation, and AI computing facilities.

Accelerating Deployment and Enhancing Sustainability

Accessen's prefabricated integrated cooling stations represent a fundamental shift in how data center cooling infrastructure is delivered. By integrating chillers, plate heat exchangers, pumps, cooling towers, valves, and intelligent control systems into a single factory-assembled and pre-tested module, Accessen reduces project deployment cycles by up to 50% compared to traditional on-site installation methods. The company's AIS (Accessen Integrated System) prefabricated integrated cooling station is designed for outdoor deployment, eliminating the need for a separate station house and enabling immediate operation upon connection to water and power on-site.

Beyond speed, Accessen's solutions deliver measurable sustainability benefits. Optimized internal piping and system design reduce energy consumption by over 20%. In landmark projects such as the Gangcheng Intelligent Manufacturing Data Park--a 90-billion-yuan, 165 MW IT capacity facility in China--Accessen's prefabricated cooling station supports an industry-leading average PUE of less than 1.25, well below the 1.55 industry baseline. The company's innovative "dual-mode" design enables seamless compatibility with both air-cooled and liquid-cooled architectures, supporting the high-density thermal requirements of AI workloads while maintaining flexibility for mixed cooling environments.

At DCWF 2026, Accessen will showcase its comprehensive portfolio, including:

  • AIS Prefabricated Integrated Cooling Stations: Outdoor modular systems that arrive fully assembled and tested, requiring only on-site utility connections for immediate operation
  • Liquid Cooling Hydraulic Modules and ACDU Coolant Distribution Units: Standardized, modular liquid cooling infrastructure designed to meet the surging cooling demands of high-density AI deployments
  • AHRI-Certified High-Efficiency Plate Heat Exchangers: Core components that deliver industry-leading thermal performance and reliability

These solutions address the full spectrum of data center cooling needs--from traditional chilled water systems to advanced liquid cooling for AI workloads--empowering operators to achieve faster time-to-market, lower operational costs, and enhanced sustainability.

Join Us in Frankfurt

"We are excited to bring Accessen's prefabricated cooling expertise to the European market at Data Centre World Frankfurt 2026," said the Accessen team. "As data center operators across Europe face increasing pressure to deploy faster while meeting stringent sustainability targets, our factory-integrated approach offers a compelling solution. With representative offices and service centers already established in Asia and expansion underway globally, we are committed to providing localized support and rapid response for our European partners and customers."

Data center operators, colocation providers, and hyperscale customers seeking to accelerate deployment timelines, reduce on-site construction complexity, and achieve ambitious sustainability goals are invited to visit Accessen at Booth M155, Hall 8 during the exhibition.

上海艾克森股份有限公司的预制化集成冷站代表了数据中心冷却基础设施交付方式的根本转变。通过将冷水机组、板式换热器、水泵、冷却塔、阀门和智能控制系统集成到一个工厂组装并预测试的模块中，上海艾克森股份有限公司可较传统现场安装方式将项目部署周期缩短最高 50%。公司的 AIS（上海艾克森股份有限公司集成系统）预制化集成冷站面向户外部署设计，无需单独建设站房，现场接通水电后即可投入运行。

  • 液冷液压模块和 ACDU 冷却液分配单元： 标准化、模块化液冷基础设施，用于满足高密度 AI 部署不断增长的冷却需求

title: Siping Juyuan Hanyang Advances Nuclear Deep-Corrugated Titanium Plate Localization

content:
A research project led by China Nuclear Power Engineering Co., Ltd., with Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. and Hunan Xiangtou Goldsky Titanium Metal Co., Ltd. as participating partners, has passed a scientific and technological achievement appraisal. The project focused on applying domestically produced titanium plate in nuclear-grade plate heat exchangers.

Key Material Progress for Nuclear Heat Exchange

Titanium plate heat exchangers are important equipment in nuclear cooling systems. Deep-corrugated plates require high-performance titanium strip with stable forming, corrosion resistance, and consistent mechanical properties. The successful appraisal indicates progress toward domestic substitution for titanium plate used in nuclear deep-corrugated plate heat exchangers.

Joint Development and Validation

The project evaluated the suitability of domestic titanium plate for nuclear-grade plate heat exchanger applications, including material behavior, plate forming, equipment manufacturing, and adaptation to nuclear operating requirements. Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. contributed from the heat exchanger equipment and engineering application side.

Toward High-End Nuclear Heat Exchange Equipment

Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. said it will continue to work on high-end nuclear heat exchange equipment and localization-oriented technical innovation. For nuclear, energy, and high-reliability industrial applications, the value of this progress lies not only in equipment delivery, but also in strengthening long-term control of critical manufacturing chains.

title: Siping Juyuan Hanyang Supplies All-Welded Plate Heat Exchangers for Arctic LNG 2
excerpt: Siping Juyuan Hanyang supplied 80 all-welded plate heat exchangers for Russia's Arctic LNG 2 project.
author: Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd.
reviewer: HeatEx Direct Editorial Team
content:
Novatek's Arctic LNG 2 natural gas liquefaction plant is a large polar LNG project. The project selected a Chinese power gas turbine supplier, and Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd., as a long-term partner in the gas turbine supply chain, supplied 80 all-welded plate heat exchangers for the project.

Heat Exchange Demand for Polar Gas Turbine Service

Arctic LNG 2 requires stable power for natural gas production, storage, condensation, and liquefaction. The onshore gas turbine power plant provides continuous electricity, while lube oil coolers and generator oil coolers are critical to reliable operation of the gas turbine system.

Validation for -52 C Conditions

The project environment can reach -52 C, placing high demands on equipment stability, reliability, and manufacturing quality. Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. developed multiple process route options and used testing to refine production methods, supporting long-term operation under severe low-temperature conditions.

80 Units Shipped to the Project

The 80 all-welded plate heat exchangers for the project have been manufactured and are being shipped to the site. The all-welded structure supports sealing reliability and is relevant for industrial applications that require low leakage risk, structural integrity, and stable long-term operation.

Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. said its product families include gasketed plate, semi-welded, all-welded, integrated heat exchange systems, and smart heating platforms. The company will continue to support domestic and overseas engineering projects through green development and technical innovation.

title: Siping Juyuan Hanyang Supported Deepwater Fleet's Equatorial Seismic Operation
excerpt: Siping Juyuan Hanyang supplied central coolers for the Haiyang Shiyou 720 and 721 geophysical vessels.
author: Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd.
reviewer: HeatEx Direct Editorial Team
content:
A Chinese deepwater geophysical fleet completed a 3D seismic exploration operation in the equatorial waters off West Africa, filling a gap in China's operating record at zero-latitude seas. The operation area was located off Gabon and covered more than 10,000 square kilometers, making it a notable marine 3D seismic exploration project.

Continuous Operation in Hot Equatorial Waters

Because the equator crosses Gabon, sea-area temperatures can reach 40 C, and marine growth creates additional operating challenges for cables, cooling systems, and long-duration vessel work. The Haiyang Shiyou 721 vessel operated continuously at sea for five months and set Chinese geophysical acquisition records for daily and monthly 3D seismic output.

Central Cooler Equipment Support

The deepwater geophysical fleet consisted of the Haiyang Shiyou 720 and Haiyang Shiyou 721 vessels. Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. supplied equipment for the related twelve-cable geophysical vessels in 2009 and 2013, including main central coolers and auxiliary central coolers, supporting the vessels' cooling systems during continuous operation.

Marine Heat Exchange Experience

Siping Juyuan Hanyang Plate Heat Exchanger Co., Ltd. has long focused on marine heat exchange applications. Its equipment can be used as central coolers, lubricating oil coolers, fresh-water coolers, and hydraulic oil coolers across tankers, LNG carriers, container ships, bulk carriers, engineering vessels, chemical tankers, asphalt carriers, deck carriers, supply vessels, and sulfur carriers.

The company said technical capability and quality assurance are key reasons marine customers select its heat exchange equipment. This case also shows the value of plate heat exchangers in marine engineering, vessel power systems, and continuous-operation cooling systems.

北极 LNG 2 项目需要稳定电力保障天然气生产、储存和冷凝液化过程。陆上燃气轮机电厂承担持续供电任务，而燃机润滑油冷却器、发电机油冷却器等换热设备，对整个燃机系统的可靠运行具有关键作用。

高温海域中的连续作业挑战

赤道横贯加蓬，作业海域温度可达 40 摄氏度，海生物滋生速度较快，对船舶拖缆、冷却系统和连续作业能力提出挑战。海洋石油 721 船海上连续作业 5 个月，并刷新我国物探三维地震采集日产、月产纪录。

中央冷却器设备支持

title: Spiral Plate Heat Exchangers: Engineering, Selection, and Market Trends
excerpt: A rewritten technical guide to spiral plate heat exchangers, covering origin, structure, welding, forming, industrial selection, competitive landscape, and China market trends.
author: HeatEx Direct Editorial Team
reviewer: HeatEx Direct Editorial Team
content:
Spiral plate heat exchangers look deceptively simple. Two long metal sheets are wound around a center, creating two separate spiral channels. One fluid enters from the center and moves outward, while the other follows the opposite path. The result is a compact counterflow heat exchanger with a flow pattern that is difficult for conventional tubular equipment to reproduce.

That geometry explains why the technology has remained relevant for nearly a century. It is especially useful when the fluid is dirty, viscous, particle-laden, or prone to fouling. Yet the same geometry also makes manufacturing quality critical: a spiral plate heat exchanger is only as good as its forming, spacing, welding, sealing, and inspection discipline.

From Invention to Industrial Platform

The modern spiral plate heat exchanger concept is commonly traced to the early twentieth century and the Rosenblad design tradition in Sweden. Its early value proposition was direct: replace bulky equipment with a compact exchanger that could provide strong counterflow heat transfer and tolerate difficult process media better than many tube bundles.

The later industrialization of the technology turned the spiral plate from a clever geometry into a repeatable pressure-vessel product. Over time, the equipment evolved from fixed, harder-to-clean units toward more maintainable designs, improved materials, automated forming, and more controlled welding methods.

Why Spiral Flow Performs Differently

In a spiral plate exchanger, each side generally follows one continuous channel. This is different from equipment with many parallel tubes or narrow plate passages, where maldistribution and dead zones can appear if the fluid contains solids or has unstable viscosity.

The curved channel produces secondary flow and wall shear. For clean liquids, that improves heat transfer. For fouling-prone streams, it can also help keep particles suspended and reduce the tendency for deposits to build up in quiet regions. This is the reason spiral plate units are often considered for refinery bottoms, slurry cooling, crystallizing liquids, wastewater concentration, pulp and paper streams, and high-viscosity process fluids.

Manufacturing Quality Is the Real Differentiator

The most important buying question is not whether a supplier can roll two plates into a spiral. It is whether the supplier can repeat the geometry, welds, and sealing quality consistently.

Key manufacturing factors include:

  • Channel spacing: small variation can create uneven velocity, local fouling, or pressure drop surprises.
  • Stud or spacer welding: spacer height, weld penetration, and distribution affect both strength and flow behavior.
  • Edge forming: smooth, consistent edges reduce dead zones and support reliable sealing.
  • Main weld quality: continuous, low-defect welds are essential for pressure integrity and cross-contamination control.
  • Heat input control: excessive heat can distort thin plate, damage corrosion resistance, or create residual stress.

Advanced suppliers use automated forming, controlled welding, inspection programs, and operating data to reduce these risks. Lower-cost suppliers may still produce usable equipment, but buyers should examine the application severity before treating all spiral plate exchangers as equivalent.

Spiral Plate Versus Shell-and-Tube

The comparison is not about declaring one technology universally better. Shell-and-tube exchangers remain strong choices for very high pressure, very clean service, simple maintenance expectations, or cost-sensitive duties. Spiral plate exchangers are more compelling when the process problem is fouling, footprint, heat recovery, or difficult liquids.

Typical spiral plate advantages include compact layout, high thermal effectiveness, a long counterflow path, and better tolerance of certain dirty or viscous streams. Typical limitations include more demanding fabrication, project-specific design work, and pressure ranges that may not match heavy tubular equipment in extreme services.

For many plants, the lifecycle economics are decisive. A spiral plate unit may cost more at purchase, but if it extends cleaning intervals, reduces unplanned shutdowns, and preserves heat recovery performance, the total operating cost can be lower.

Where Spiral Plate Heat Exchangers Fit Best

Strong candidate services include:

  • Refinery and petrochemical streams with heavy hydrocarbons or suspended solids.
  • Pulp, paper, and fiber-containing process liquids.
  • Wastewater and evaporation duties with scaling tendency.
  • Mineral processing slurry and hydrometallurgical liquids.
  • Compact heat recovery projects where space is limited.
  • Valuable or hazardous media where welded construction is preferred.

Less suitable cases include ultra-high-pressure duties, very clean utility fluids where a simpler exchanger is cheaper, or processes where extremely low pressure drop is more important than heat transfer intensity.

Competitive Landscape and China Market Direction

International brands have accumulated decades of design data, manufacturing routines, and service knowledge. Their strength is not only equipment geometry; it is the combination of repeatable production, materials experience, inspection culture, and lifecycle support.

Chinese manufacturers have moved from early imitation and standardization toward broader domestic production and selected high-end applications. The market now shows a familiar split: premium projects tend to value proven references and quality systems, while lower-risk duties often prioritize price and delivery speed.

For Chinese suppliers, the next stage is likely to depend on specialization rather than broad imitation. Stronger positions can come from mastering a narrow set of duties, building real test data, improving welding automation, documenting lifecycle performance, and offering service beyond the initial equipment sale.

Quote Request Checklist for Buyers

When requesting a spiral plate exchanger quotation, include more than flow rate and inlet/outlet temperatures. A useful quote request should also describe fouling mechanism, solids content, particle size, viscosity curve, corrosive species, cleaning method, allowable pressure drop, operating cycle target, inspection requirements, and material preferences.

Ask suppliers to explain channel gap selection, weld inspection, mechanical cleaning access, pressure vessel code compliance, and comparable references. These answers will reveal more than a low initial price.

Takeaway

Spiral plate heat exchangers are not general-purpose replacements for every heat exchanger. They are specialized tools for duties where compact counterflow heat transfer, dirty-fluid tolerance, and long operating cycles matter.

The best projects treat spiral plate technology as an engineered system: flow behavior, welding, forming, cleaning, material selection, and service support must be evaluated together. When those pieces align, the spiral plate exchanger can solve problems that conventional equipment only manages through oversizing, frequent cleaning, or lost heat recovery.

title: 螺旋板式换热器工程、选型与市场趋势指南
excerpt: 一篇重新撰写的螺旋板式换热器技术指南，覆盖起源、结构、焊接、成型、工业选型、竞争格局和中国市场趋势。
author: HeatEx Direct 编辑团队
reviewer: HeatEx Direct 编辑团队
content:
螺旋板式换热器看起来并不复杂：两张长金属板围绕中心卷制，形成两条相互隔离的螺旋通道。一侧流体从中心进入并向外流动，另一侧则按相反方向通过。最终形成的是一种紧凑的逆流换热器，其流动形态很难被传统管式设备完全复制。

这种几何结构解释了为什么螺旋板技术在近百年后仍然有价值。它尤其适合处理脏污、高黏度、含颗粒或易结垢介质。但同样因为结构特殊，制造质量也变得非常关键：一台螺旋板式换热器的可靠性，取决于成型、间距、焊接、密封和检验能否稳定受控。

从发明到工业平台

现代螺旋板式换热器通常可追溯到 20 世纪早期的瑞典 Rosenblad 技术体系。其早期价值主张很清楚：用紧凑设备替代笨重换热器，在提供强逆流传热的同时，更好地适应部分管束设备难处理的复杂介质。

后续的工业化过程，把螺旋板从一个巧妙几何结构变成了可重复制造的压力容器产品。随着时间推移，设备从早期不可拆、清洗困难的形式，逐步发展出更可维护的结构、更丰富的材料、更自动化的成型工艺，以及更受控的焊接方法。

螺旋流道为什么不同

在螺旋板换热器中，两侧通常各自沿一条连续通道流动。这不同于多根并联管束或窄板片通道，因为后者在介质含固体或黏度波动时更容易出现分配不均和死区。

弯曲通道会诱导二次流和壁面剪切。对清洁液体而言，这会强化传热；对易结垢流体而言，它还有助于保持颗粒悬浮，降低沉积物在低速区域堆积的倾向。这也是螺旋板常被用于炼油重质物料、浆液冷却、结晶液、废水浓缩、制浆造纸和高黏度工艺流体的原因。

制造质量才是核心差异

采购时最重要的问题，并不是供应商能否把两张板卷成螺旋，而是能否稳定重复通道几何、焊缝质量和密封质量。

关键制造因素包括：

  • 通道间距：细小偏差也可能造成流速不均、局部结垢或压降异常。
  • 定距柱或支撑件焊接：高度、熔深和分布会同时影响强度和流动行为。
  • 边缘成型：平滑、稳定的边缘可以减少死区，并提升密封可靠性。
  • 主焊缝质量：连续、低缺陷焊缝对承压完整性和防止串漏至关重要。
  • 热输入控制：过高热输入会使薄板变形、削弱耐腐蚀性或引入残余应力。

成熟供应商通常会通过自动成型、受控焊接、检验程序和运行数据来降低这些风险。低成本供应商也可能做出可用设备，但采购方应根据工况严苛程度判断，不能把所有螺旋板换热器视为同一等级。

螺旋板与管壳式如何比较

这个问题并不是简单判断谁更先进。管壳式换热器在超高压、清洁介质、维护要求简单或预算敏感场景中仍然很有竞争力。螺旋板式换热器更适合解决结垢、占地、热回收或复杂液体流动问题。

螺旋板的典型优势包括结构紧凑、热效率高、逆流路径长，以及对某些脏污或黏性介质更友好。其典型限制则包括制造要求高、设计更依赖项目工况，以及在极端高压场景下未必能替代重型管式设备。

对很多工厂来说，生命周期成本才是决定因素。螺旋板设备初始采购价可能更高，但如果它能延长清洗周期、减少非计划停机并保持热回收效率，总运行成本反而可能更低。

哪些工况更适合螺旋板

更适合考虑螺旋板的场景包括：

  • 炼油和石化行业中的重质烃类或含固体流体。
  • 制浆造纸及含纤维工艺液。
  • 有结垢倾向的废水和蒸发浓缩工况。
  • 矿物加工浆液与湿法冶金液体。
  • 空间受限的紧凑型热回收项目。
  • 需要焊接结构的贵重或危险介质。

不太适合的场景包括超高压工况、极其清洁且更适合低成本方案的公用工程介质，或压降要求远高于传热强度的流程。

竞争格局与中国市场方向

国际品牌在设计数据、制造流程和服务经验方面有长期积累。它们的优势不只是设备形状，而是可重复生产、材料经验、检验文化和生命周期支持的组合。

中国制造商则经历了从早期仿制、标准化到本土化生产和部分高端应用突破的过程。当前市场呈现明显分层：高端项目更看重项目业绩和质量体系，风险较低的应用则常常更关注价格和交期。

对中国供应商而言，下一阶段更可能依赖专业化，而不是广泛模仿。更稳固的竞争力来自聚焦少数细分工况、建立真实测试数据、提升焊接自动化、记录全生命周期表现，并把服务能力延伸到设备交付之后。

采购 询价应包含什么

询价螺旋板换热器时，不应只提供流量和进出口温度。更有价值的询价资料 还应说明结垢机理、固含量、粒径、黏度曲线、腐蚀性组分、清洗方式、允许压降、目标运行周期、检验要求和材料偏好。

采购方还应要求供应商解释通道间距选择、焊缝检验、机械清洗通道、压力容器规范符合性以及相近项目业绩。这些回答往往比低报价更能反映真实能力。

小结

螺旋板式换热器不是所有换热场景的通用替代品。它更像是一种专用工具，适用于紧凑逆流传热、脏污介质适应性和长周期运行都很重要的工况。

成功项目不会只把螺旋板看成一个设备外形，而会把它作为完整工程系统评估：流动行为、焊接、成型、清洗、材料选择和服务支持必须一起判断。当这些条件匹配时，螺旋板换热器可以解决传统设备只能通过放大尺寸、频繁清洗或牺牲热回收来勉强处理的问题。

reviewer: 上海艾克森股份有限公司
content:
由上海艾克森股份有限公司参与起草的 NB/T 11748-2024《板式空冷器》行业标准已正式发布。该标准由国家能源局批准、全国锅炉压力容器标准化技术委员会换热器分技术委员会归口管理，将于 2025 年 6 月 25 日实施。作为该领域首个行业标准，它对板式空冷器制造和检验的全生命周期提出系统规范，是行业标准化进程中的重要里程碑。

板式空冷器是一种用于汽/水、气/气工况的高效换热设备，融合了板式换热器和空冷器的特点，通过空气与流体的直接或间接接触实现热量传递，尤其适用于高温及余热回收场景。该设备以全焊接板束作为传热单元，具备结构紧凑、传热效率高、压降低等优势，在炼化、化工、电力、冶金等行业的烟气余热回收中发挥关键作用。

随着市场需求增长和应用场景拓展，统一行业标准已成为必要。该标准由换热器分技术委员会牵头制定，中国特种设备检测研究院、中国石化、西安交通大学、成达工程、中国石油、哈尔滨空调等单位共同参与。凭借二十余年板式空气预热器研发与制造经验，上海艾克森股份有限公司为标准起草提供了关键技术支撑。作为国家标准制定的长期参与者，上海艾克森股份有限公司通过板式换热器、A-BLOC 四侧可拆焊接换热器、AWK 全焊接空气换热器等产品组合提供了重要技术验证。

NB/T 11748-2024 标准规定：设计压力不大于 4.0 MPa，温度范围根据材料确定。标准通过严格要求覆盖设备全生命周期：

  • 材料选择：金属和非金属材料的性能指标
  • 设计：热力与机械设计方法
  • 制造：焊接工艺和板束装配规程
  • 检验与验收：无损检测、压力试验、泄漏试验和运行验证
  • 性能评价：能效指标与噪声评估方法

该标准还提供故障诊断指南和纠正措施，以保障设备长期可靠运行。

content:
The NB/T 11748-2024 "Plate Air Cooler" industry standard, co-drafted by Shanghai Accessen, has been officially released. Approved by the National Energy Administration and administered by the Heat Exchanger Subcommittee of the China Standardization Committee for Boilers and Pressure Vessels, this inaugural standard will take effect on June 25, 2025. It establishes comprehensive specifications for the entire lifecycle of plate air cooler manufacturing and inspection, marking a critical milestone for industry standardization.

As a high-efficiency heat exchange device for steam/water and gas/gas applications, plate air coolers integrate features of plate heat exchangers and air-cooled exchangers. They transfer heat through direct/indirect air-to-fluid contact, excelling in high-temperature and heat recovery applications. Utilizing fully-welded plate bundles as thermal transfer units, these systems offer compact design, superior heat transfer efficiency, and low pressure drop--delivering critical performance in heat recovery from flue gases across refining, chemical, power, and metallurgical industries.

Rising market demand and expanding applications necessitate unified industry standards. Led by the Heat Exchanger Subcommittee, the standard was developed with participation from China Special Equipment Inspection Institute, Sinopec, Xi'an Jiaotong University, Chengda Engineering, PetroChina, and Harbin Air Conditioning. Leveraging over two decades of expertise in plate air preheater R&D and manufacturing, Shanghai Accessen contributed pivotal technical insights to the drafting process. As a veteran participant in national standard formulation, Accessen provided critical technical validation through its portfolio: plate heat exchangers, A-BLOC four-side accessible welded exchangers, and AWK fully-welded air heat exchangers.

The NB/T 11748-2024 standard specifies: Design pressure limit: ≤4.0 MPa, Temperature range: Material-dependent. It governs the entire equipment lifecycle through rigorous requirements for:

  • Material Selection: Performance metrics for metallic/non-metallic materials
  • Design: Thermal and mechanical design methodologies
  • Manufacturing: Welding procedures and plate bundle assembly protocols
  • Inspection & Acceptance: NDT, pressure testing, leak testing, operational validation
  • Performance Evaluation: Energy efficiency metrics and noise assessment methodologies

The standard further provides fault diagnosis guidelines and corrective measures to ensure long-term operational reliability.

Accessen's contribution to this standard provides definitive technical guidance for industry advancement. Its plate air preheaters have delivered significant economic and environmental benefits in over 20 projects, including:

  • DeNOx systems for CO converters at Sinopec Yangzi Aromatic Plant

These implementations empower clients to achieve cost reduction, efficiency gains, and emission cuts in clean energy transitions.

title: 7 Essential Steps to Keep Your Heat Exchanger Efficient and Reduce Costs!
excerpt: Reducing costs is a top priority for every factory, and equipment engineers play a key role in achieving this goal. One effective method is to identify and address bottlenecks in the proces…
author: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
reviewer: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
content:
Reducing costs is a top priority for every factory, and equipment engineers play a key role in achieving this goal. One effective method is to identify and address bottlenecks in the process. This is especially important for heat exchangers, as operational interruptions can lead to expensive downtime. To help prevent such losses, here are seven key areas to focus on:

STEP 1: Monitor Pressure Drop

Monitoring the pressure drop in the heat exchanger is a critical step that cannot be ignored. Heat exchangers are designed to operate at specific pressure drop levels, and any deviation can cause various problems. An increase in pressure drop indicates an issue that needs immediate attention.

Equipment engineers should stop the operation immediately and investigate the root cause of the pressure drop to take necessary corrective actions. Ignoring this issue can lead to a series of problems, ultimately causing production delays and equipment failure.

STEP 2: Plan for Spare Parts

Imagine if a heat exchanger suddenly stops during production. If you have a spare plate pack on hand, you can quickly replace the faulty part and resume operation. However, if there are no spare parts available, you would have to order from the factory, which can take weeks or even months to arrive. This downtime results in significant time and financial costs for the factory.

Therefore, it is essential to have spare parts or alternative solutions readily available. It is the responsibility of the equipment engineer to ensure that the necessary resources are in place to manage unexpected problems. Keeping spare plate packs near the heat exchanger is one of the most effective ways to ensure smooth operation.

STEP 3: Professional Routine Maintenance

Like other equipment, heat exchangers require regular maintenance to maintain efficient operation. However, attempting to maintain a heat exchanger without proper expertise can lead to poor performance or even damage to the equipment.

Using professional heat exchanger maintenance services can ensure that the equipment always operates efficiently. Experts can also identify any inefficiencies in the current setup and suggest optimizations for the heat exchanger’s performance.

STEP 4: Monitor Heat Exchanger Parameters

Unfortunately, you cannot directly observe the interior of a heat exchanger to monitor its performance. However, you can still "diagnose" it by regularly checking pressure drop and heat exchange efficiency. Sudden changes in these parameters may indicate problems that require immediate attention. Do not ignore these changes or hope they disappear on their own.

If left unchecked, issues like scaling and corrosion can result in reduced efficiency, increased energy costs, and equipment failure. Regular monitoring helps identify and resolve these issues early.

Professional Tip:

Re-evaluating a heat exchanger requires expertise in thermal, fluid dynamics, and material science. It is crucial to involve experienced professionals to ensure that the recalculated equipment meets performance specifications, safety standards, and regulatory requirements.

Shanghai Heat Transfer's "Smart Eye" system utilizes advanced technologies like IoT, AI, and big data for comprehensive monitoring, analysis, diagnosis, and alerting of plate heat exchanger conditions. This system guides users to optimize operation, extend equipment lifespan, reduce maintenance costs, and maximize energy efficiency.

STEP 5: Refurbishment Services

Heat exchangers are a significant investment for factories, so it makes sense to maximize their use. However, sometimes a heat exchanger may no longer be suitable for its initial purpose. In such cases, buying a new one is not always the best option; old heat exchangers can be refurbished for a new use.

In other words, you can re-evaluate on-site equipment for alternative purposes. This process includes recalculating heat transfer area, fluid velocity, pressure drop, and gasket material to make adjustments based on new requirements. By recalculating, the heat exchanger can meet the factory’s current needs, helping you save on the costs associated with purchasing new equipment.

STEP 6: Address Leaks Immediately

Leaks in heat exchangers are a common issue that can lead to contamination and equipment failure. If you notice a leak, it needs to be addressed immediately to prevent further damage.

Leaks can occur both internally and externally in the heat exchanger, requiring different corrective actions. Internal leaks typically indicate problems with the plates and need immediate replacement to prevent cross-contamination of the fluids.

On the other hand, external leaks usually point to gasket issues, and replacing the gaskets can resolve the problem.

STEP 7: Assemble the Heat Exchanger Correctly

Assembling a heat exchanger may seem easy, but it requires careful attention to detail. Following the operation instructions is crucial to ensure optimal performance.

Pay close attention to the bevel and code on the front of the plates during assembly. Incorrect assembly can lead to decreased performance or increased pressure drop. Additionally, avoid applying too much force when pressing the plates, as this could cause them to crack. Take your time and ensure the plates are correctly aligned and secured.

Professional Tip:

Heat transfer efficiency is not the ultimate goal. We must always consider cost.

title: Advanced Analysis on Wide-Gap Welded Plate Heat Exchanger: Core Processes & Industrial Practice
excerpt: Conventional heat transfer equipment often faces critical challenges in thermal efficiency and operational reliability when processing high-viscosity, high-solid and heavy-fouling media. Th…
author: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
reviewer: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
content:
Conventional heat transfer equipment often faces critical challenges in thermal efficiency and operational reliability when processing high-viscosity, high-solid and heavy-fouling media.

This document comprehensively analyzes the design philosophy, advanced manufacturing processes and typical industrial applications of SHPHE’s wide-gap welded plate heat exchanger(WGPHE).Equipped with a unique free-flow non-clogging channel structure, advanced resistance seam welding technology, as well as fluid dynamic optimization based on the field coordination principle, the equipment achieves high-efficiency heat transfer and stable blockage-free operation under harsh operating conditions.

1. The Engineering Paradox: Efficiency vs. Reliability

Industrial processes handling slurries (alumina, mining), fibers media(pulp and paper), and high-viscosity fluids (sugar, ethanol) often face a inherent tradeoff between operational continuity and heat transfer efficiency.

Failure Modes of Conventional Equipment

  • Shell and Tube Exchanger: Laminar flow tendencies can reduce the overall heat transfer coefficient K.In addition, their specific surface area is typically around 100 m²/m³, leading to large installation footprint and high alloy material consumption. Dead zones on the shell side promote solids sedimentation and accelerate under deposit corrosion.

  • Gasketed Plate Heat Exchanger (GPHE): Polymer gaskets suffer from service failure at temperatures above 180 °C or pressures exceeding 2.5 MPa. Despite high compactness with a specific surface area exceeding 2000 m²/m³, narrow channels of 2 mm to 4 mm and dense chevron contact structures create a filtration effect, easily causing blockage of fibers and solid particles.

2. The WGPHE Solution

WGPHE overcomes these limitations with optimized structural design focused on unobstructed flow and long-term durability.

  • Variable wide channel: The variable wide channel design of 8 mm to 30 mm accommodates media with high solid content, long fibers and high-viscosity fluids, enabling unobstructed flow in plug flow or turbulent flow conditions and effectively reducing clogging risks.

  • Fully-welded structure: Full welding technology extends operational limits up to 350 °C and 3.5 MPa.

  • Free-flow design: The free-flow design minimizes contact points, effectively reducing clogging risks.

3. Core Physics: Deep Integration of Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer

WGPHE employs specialized plate geometry to modulate the fluid boundary layer and sustain high heat transfer efficiency, quantified by the Nusselt number, even at low flow velocities.

A) High-solid Slurries (Alumina, Sewage Sludge)

Fluid Mechanics Mechanism: Dimpled plate structures induce boundary layer separation and generate strong secondary flows such as longitudinal and shedding vortices at low flow velocities. This enhances radial mixing and wall shear.

Thermodynamic Integration Effect:

  • Radial Mixing: Secondary flows continuously carry central fluid to the heated wall and redistribute wall fluid inward, breaking laminar heat transfer limitations and greatly improving radial heat transport.

  • Self-cleaning Performance: Vortex-induced shear force scours the plate surface, preventing particle deposition and maintaining unobstructed flow and stable heat transfer.

B) Fibrous Media (Papermaking, Sugar Production)

Fluid Dynamics Mechanism:The column-protruded plate design forms free flow channels without continuous contact lines via discrete column supports, preventing fiber adhesion on the wall. As fluid flows around the columns, stable Kármán vortex streets are generated within an appropriate Reynolds number range (approximately 40–200).

Thermodynamic Integration Effect:

  • Periodic Disturbance Heat Transfer: The protruding columns introduce continuous periodic flow disturbances, effectively disrupting the thermal boundary layer and significantly enhancing heat transfer.

  • Shear Scour Anti-fouling Effect: Alternating vortex shedding behind the columns creates unsteady transverse pressure fluctuations and shear forces. This produces a sustained scouring and cleaning effect on fibers and soft deposits, achieving dynamic integration of high heat transfer and stable anti-clogging performance.

C) High-Viscosity / Non-Newtonian Fluids (Ethanol Mash, Waste Liquids)

Fluid Dynamics Mechanism

High-viscosity fluids have low Reynolds numbers and exhibit laminar flow in smooth channels. Wide channels combined with dimpled or column-shaped plates act as fixed vortex generators, inducing fluid separation, reattachment and vortex flow.

Heat Transfer Enhancement

  • Field Synergy Optimization：According to the field synergy principle, heat transfer efficiency depends on the vector angle between velocity and temperature gradient. Laminar flow has poor synergy due to near-vertical alignment. The three-dimensional flow from plate structures adjusts flow direction, reduces local angular deviation, and improves the synergy coefficient, achieving high Nusselt numbers at low flow speeds.

  • Non-Newtonian Fluid Adaptation：For shear-thinning fluids, high shear in vortex regions reduces apparent viscosity, improving fluid flow and heat transfer performance.

D) Asymmetric Heat Transfer Requirements (Steam Heating, Rich-Liquid Heat Recovery)

Integrated Fluid Dynamics and Heat Transfer Design

Breaking symmetric design principles, asymmetric channels are customized to match fluid heat transfer characteristics (condensation vs. single-phase flow, clean vs. fouling media) and hydraulic properties (pressure drop, viscosity).

Example: Steam heating of ethanol mash

  • Steam side (narrow channel): Narrow passages increase flow velocity to leverage high condensation heat transfer of steam.

  • Mash side (wide channel): Wide channels prevent blockage, while optimized plate geometry compensates for heat transfer reduction.

System-level optimization:Differential channel design balances thermal resistance on both sides, maximizing the overall heat transfer coefficient (K), which is unachievable with conventional symmetric designs.

4. Advanced Manufacturing

The reliability of wide-channel fully welded heat exchangers relies on precise control of resistance welding parameters.

Advantages of Resistance Seam Welding: Precision, Reliability and Efficiency

Resistance seam welding applies electrode pressure and current to generate resistance heat, achieving metallurgical bonding of plates for WGPHE:

High-efficiency production and consistent quality：Continuous high-speed welding enables integrated channel sealing. Precise parameter control ensures consistent weld strength and tightness for long-term operation.

Superior mechanical and sealing performance：Dense metallurgical joints match base material strength, with pressure resistance up to 3.5 MPa. The seamless structure prevents leakage, suitable for hazardous and high-value media. The gasket-free design supports temperatures up to 350 °C.

Cost-effectiveness and low maintenance:Elimination of gasket replacement reduces maintenance and downtime. The compact design minimizes volume for equivalent heat transfer performance.

5. Material Adaptability and Anti-Corrosion & Wear Resistance Strategy

Facing complex corrosive and abrasive conditions in the chemical industry, SHPHE has established a comprehensive processing system for special materials.

  • Super Austenitic and Duplex Steel (254SMO, 2205, 2507)：Ideal for high-chloride environments such as seawater cooling and papermaking bleaching liquor with excellent pitting resistance (PREN > 40).For high-solids and abrasive media like alumina, duplex steel provides superior hardness and abrasion resistance.

  • Nickel Alloys (Hastelloy C-276, C-22)：Specially applied for high-temperature concentrated sulfuric acid, mixed acids and fluorine-containing waste liquids.Advanced laser welding parameters ensure crack-free welds for nickel alloy components.

  • Titanium (Gr.1, Gr.2)：Offers outstanding corrosion resistance in extreme oxidizing environments and seawater applications.Inert gas shielded welding is adopted to prevent hydrogen embrittlement at high temperatures.

Conclusion

SHPHE’s WGPHE realize systematic integration of fluid dynamics, heat transfer and material processing technologies. They effectively solve heat transfer challenges of high-viscosity, high-solid and fouling-prone media, combining smooth flow performance with high heat transfer efficiency.Widely used in alumina slurry cooling, sugar processing, fuel ethanol production and black liquor recovery, the equipment serves as a key energy-saving solution to support the low-carbon strategy.

Pushing the Physical Limits of Industrial Processes

In today’s advanced equipment manufacturing and energy and chemical sectors, engineers are facing unprecedented extreme challenges. From subsea oil and gas production in water depths up to 3,000 m to hydrogen fuel refueling stations with pressures as high as 70 MPa, and further to fourth generation nuclear energy and supercritical power generation systems pursuing ultimate thermal efficiency, traditional heat exchange equipment can no longer adapt to these extreme operating conditions. Traditional shell and tube heat exchangers, while technologically mature, require exponentially thicker shell walls when handling high pressure media. This leads to massive equipment size and astonishing weight, making it impossible to meet the stringent lightweight requirements of offshore equipment. On the other hand, plate heat exchangers, whether gasketed or welded, are compact, but the nature of their plates and sealing structures means they cannot withstand pressures beyond 10 MPa or extremely high temperatures. Against this backdrop, the Printed Circuit Heat Exchanger (PCHE) emerged as a tailored solution. Benefiting from its precision-engineered thermal channel design and two core manufacturing processes—chemical etching and vacuum diffusion bonding—the PCHE achieves three major performance breakthroughs: ultra-high pressure resistance, tolerance to extreme temperature differentials, and an exceptionally compact structure. From an engineering application perspective, this paper presents an in-depth analysis of the application of PCHE developed by Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. across key scenarios including hydrogen energy and offshore oil and gas.

Hydrogen Energy Infrastructure: Managing High Pressure and Pre-Cooling Duty

Hydrogen energy is recognized as the ultimate clean energy. However, hydrogen’s intrinsic physical properties—extreme difficulty in compression and high leakage propensity—impose near-stringent requirements on core heat exchange equipment. With its unique design and manufacturing features, Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.’s PCHE has become the core equipment for addressing high-pressure and cryogenic challenges in hydrogen energy applications.

Engineering Challenges of Hydrogen Refueling Station (HRS) Pre-cooling Systems

To extend the driving range of fuel cell vehicles, mainstream international refueling standards require high-pressure fast refueling at 70 MPa. The core technical challenge lies in this requirement: the heat exchanger must withstand ultra-high operating pressures—with a typical design pressure of 100 MPa—and tolerate severe pressure and temperature cycling. The PCHE developed by Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. features a maximum design pressure of up to 100 MPa, delivering reliable safety assurance for 70 MPa refueling operations. Its seamless core structure, formed through the diffusion bonding process, fundamentally eliminates the risk of leakage under high-pressure conditions.

Material selection: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. utilizes 316L austenitic stainless steel or nickel-based alloys. These materials have excellent resistance to hydrogen embrittlement in high pressure hydrogen environments, effectively preventing hydrogen atoms from penetrating the metal lattice and causing brittle fracture.

Structural fatigue resistance: The base metal diffusion bonding of PCHE endows it with exceptional fatigue life. This enables the unit to withstand tens of thousands of pressure charge-discharge cycles throughout the full-service life of a hydrogen refueling station.

Offshore Oil and Gas Engineering: Reducing the Footprint on Valuable Deck Space

On deep sea FPSOs (Floating Production, Storage and Offloading units) or drilling platforms, space and payload are highly cost-intensive resources. Every additional ton of weight added to a platform will significantly increase the cost of its underlying floating structure.

Process Pain Point: Handling High-Pressure Natural Gas

Natural gas extracted from deep-sea operations features an extremely high pressure ranging from 10 to 20 MPa, typically coupled with high temperature and high humidity. Prior to pipeline transportation or liquefaction, it must undergo dehydration, heavy hydrocarbon removal, and interstage compressor cooling. If a shell and tube heat exchanger is adopted, its shell wall thickness must be excessively large to withstand 20 MPa pressures. When considering the flooded weight, the equipment’s operational weight often reaches hundreds of tons. This not only takes up valuable deck space but also presents enormous challenges to the platform’s center-of-gravity control and structural support systems. The heat transfer compactness of Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.’s PCHE can reach up to 2500 m²/m³, with its weight reduced by approximately 80% compared to conventional shell and tube heat exchangers.

Summary

In summary, Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.’s PCHE products are not merely single-function heat exchangers, but comprehensive thermal solutions tailored specifically for extreme industrial scenarios.

  • Design pressure and temperature: With a pressure resistance of 100 MPa and temperature tolerance of 850°C, Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.’s PCHE boasts distinct technological leadership advantages.
  • Manufacturing processes: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. has mastered the etching and welding processes for a diverse range of materials—from 304/316L austenitic stainless steels to seawater-resistant titanium, and nickel-based alloys suitable for high-temperature and highly corrosive media.
  • Manufacturing scale: A single unit can deliver a heat exchange area of up to 8,000 m², demonstrating Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.’s capability to support large-scale oil and gas and power projects.
  • Customization services: Leveraging the flexibility of chemical etching, Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. can provide customers with fully customized channel configurations to achieve the optimal balance between pressure drop and heat transfer efficiency.

excerpt: Floating Liquefied Natural Gas (FLNG) facilities serve as the core equipment for the development of deep-sea natural gas resources. By integrating the entire onshore natural gas processing…
author: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
reviewer: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
content:
Floating Liquefied Natural Gas (FLNG) facilities serve as the core equipment for the development of deep-sea natural gas resources. By integrating the entire onshore natural gas processing flow onto a mobile offshore platform, FLNG enables the integrated operation of natural gas covering extraction, purification, liquefaction, storage, and offloading.

1. Core Process Flow of FLNG Platforms

The primary process flow of an FLNG platform can be refined into five critical stages:

  1. Feed Gas Extraction and Transport: Raw natural gas is extracted from deep-sea wells via subsea trees and transported to the FLNG platform through subsea flowlines. The feed gas typically arrives at an initial pressure of 1–10 MPa, with temperatures ranging from 4 to 12 °C,  depending on the subsea environment.
  2. Feed Gas Pre-treatment: To prevent corrosion, freezing/blockage, and reduced liquefaction efficiency in downstream equipment, the gas undergoes rigorous purification:
    • Amine Scrubbing: For decarbonization (CO2 removal).
    • Alcohol-Amine Process: For desulfurization (H2S removal).
    • Molecular Sieve Dehydration: For removing water, trace heavy hydrocarbons, and mercury.
    • Target Specifications: CO2 < 50 ppm, H2S < 6 mg/m³, and H2O ≤ 1 ppm.
  3. Natural Gas Compression: Multi-stage centrifugal compressors boost the purified natural gas pressure to 4–10 MPa required for liquefaction. Due to the adiabatic compression effect, gas temperatures rise to 80–120°C, necessitating cooling via heat exchangers before the next stage.
  4. Natural Gas Liquefaction: This is the heart of the process. Using the Mixed Refrigerant Cycle (MRC), a mixed refrigerant (comprising methane, ethane, propane, nitrogen, etc.) is compressed, cooled, and throttled to create a cryogenic source. This refrigerant exchanges heat efficiently with high-pressure purified natural gas in the liquefier, cooling the gas to -162°C at atmospheric pressure. This phase change transforms it from gas to liquid LNG, reducing its volume to approximately 1/600 of the original.
  5. LNG Storage and Offloading: The liquefied LNG is stored in the platform’s built-in cryogenic adiabatic tanks, maintained at -162°C and 0.1–0.2 MPa. It is then transferred via loading arms to LNG carriers, achieving the offshore export of deep-sea natural gas resources.

2. Challenges for Heat Exchangers in FLNG Applications

FLNG platforms operate in harsh offshore environments, imposing strict demands on core heat transfer equipment:

  • With limited deck space and load capacity, FLNG layouts are highly compact.
  • High salt spray, high humidity and marine atmospheric corrosion demand superior corrosion resistance and fatigue strength for heat exchangers.
  • Core processes such as natural gas liquefaction and BOG (Boil-Off Gas) recovery require efficient heat transfer. The presence of gas-liquid two-phase flow during heat exchange imposes high requirements on thermal efficiency and flow field stability.
  • FLNG operations require high continuity and safety, which necessitates heat exchange equipment with long-term stable operation capability and convenient maintenance.

3. Advantages of PCHE

  1. Superior compactness: PCHE uses micro-channel structures with millimeter-scale flow passages, achieving a heat transfer area density of up to 2500 m²/m³. Efficiency is 3-5 times higher than traditional shell-and-tube exchangers, while volume and weight are reduced to 1/10 and 1/5 respectively, effectively solving space and load constraints.
  2. Excellent structural strength, corrosion resistance, and fatigue resistance: PCHE is made of stainless steel or nickel-based alloy, and its core is formed by an integral diffusion bonding process. Strength reaches 95% of the base metal, with no weld leakage risk. The material has good resistance to marine salt spray corrosion, and the integrated structure can withstand alternating loads and impact vibration, giving it better fatigue life than traditional heat exchangers.
  3. Strong adaptability to working conditions: The microchannel design can flexibly adapt to gas-liquid two-phase flow, a wide temperature range (-196°C to +850°C), and a wide pressure range (0.1-100 MPa). In heat exchange scenarios such as cryogenic liquefaction and BOG recovery, it offers uniform temperature, low flow resistance, and strong heat exchange stability.
  4. Convenient operation and maintenance: PCHE adopts a modular design that can be flexibly combined according to process requirements. It is easy to install and disassemble, significantly reducing operation and maintenance costs and shutdown risks on FLNG offshore platforms.

4. Application of PCHE on FLNG Platforms

Due to its technical characteristics, PCHE has become the optimal choice for multiple critical heat transfer units on FLNG platforms.

Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. solutions are widely applied in the following critical positions:

  1. Natural Gas Cooler (Feed Gas Pre-treatment)
    • Function: Cools raw gas to stabilize conditions for purification.
    • Cold Side: Seawater (15–35°C, 0.1–0.5 MPa).
    • Hot Side: Raw Natural Gas (Inlet: 40–60°C, Outlet: 20–40°C, 1–5 MPa).
  2. Compressor Aftercooler (Compression Stage)
    • Function: Removes adiabatic heat generated during compression.
    • Cold Side: Seawater (15–35°C, 0.1–0.5 MPa).
    • Hot Side: Compressed Natural Gas (Inlet: 80–120°C, Outlet: 30–40°C, 5–10 MPa).
  3. Natural Gas Liquefier (Core Liquefaction Stage)
    • Function: Serves as the core equipment for converting high-pressure gas into LNG.
    • Cold Side: Mixed Refrigerant (-100 to -162°C, 1–5 MPa).
    • Hot Side: Purified High-Pressure Gas (Inlet: 20–40°C, Outlet: -162°C, 4–10 MPa).
  4. BOG Heat Exchanger (Storage & Recovery Stage)
    • Function: Re-liquefies Boil-Off Gas (BOG) using LNG cold energy to reduce loss and emissions.
    • Cold Side: LNG (-162°C, 0.7–2 MPa).
    • Hot Side: BOG Gas (-10 to 20°C, 0.5–4 MPa).
  5. High-Pressure and Low-Pressure Vaporizer
    • Function: Regasifies LNG to platform power and instrumentation fuel.
    • Cold Side: LNG (-162°C, 0.1–0.2 MPa).
    • Hot Side: Seawater/Air/Glycol Water (5–25°C, up to 10 MPa for high-pressure types).

The products can stably withstand a pressure of 100 MPa and extreme temperatures (-196°C to +850°C), adapting to the cryogenic and high-pressure working conditions of FLNG. A plate heat exchanger skid is an integrated system featuring a plate heat exchanger as its core component, combined with pumps, valves, instruments, piping, and a PLC control system, all pre-installed on a steel base skid. This modular system can be easily transported, positioned, and connected to other equipment via flanges for immediate use.

By leveraging modular integration, factory pre-assembly, and intelligent management, plate heat exchanger skids solve the traditional challenges of complex installation, difficult maintenance, and poor adaptability. They have become a critical solution in industries such as marine, oil and gas, chemical processing, and renewable energy. Their core value lies in improving construction efficiency and reducing lifecycle costs, especially in harsh environments, rapid deployment scenarios, or space-constrained settings.

Key Applications of Plate Heat Exchanger Skids in Marine Engineering

Seawater Cooling Systems

On large vessels such as cruise ships, LNG carriers, and container ships, engines and machinery generate large amounts of heat. High-temperature freshwater circulates to absorb this heat and then transfers it to low-temperature freshwater via plate heat exchanger skids. The low-temperature water is subsequently cooled by seawater in seawater coolers, maintaining optimal operating temperatures for ship equipment.

Freshwater Supply Systems

On offshore platforms, plate heat exchanger skids play a vital role in seawater desalination. Before reverse osmosis treatment, seawater is heated to the optimal temperature using a heat exchanger skid to improve membrane efficiency. After desalination, freshwater can also be cooled or heated as needed to meet living and production requirements.

HVAC Systems

Plate heat exchanger skids are crucial in marine HVAC systems. They facilitate heat transfer for indoor climate control: heating interior spaces in winter by transferring heat from hot water to air, and cooling spaces in summer by transferring indoor heat to chilled water, ensuring comfortable living and working environments on offshore platforms.

Crude Oil Processing Systems

In offshore oil extraction, crude oil often contains large amounts of water and impurities. Before dewatering and desalting, plate heat exchanger skids preheat the crude oil to improve processing efficiency. After treatment, the oil is cooled by skids for easier storage and transportation.

Hydraulic Systems

Marine engineering relies heavily on hydraulic machinery, including cranes and drilling equipment. During operation, hydraulic oil heats up because of friction. Plate heat exchanger skids dissipate this heat, maintaining stable oil temperature and ensuring hydraulic system reliability and performance.

Marine Aquaculture Facilities

In marine aquaculture, especially for temperature-sensitive species, removable plate heat exchanger skids are used to control water temperature. By exchanging heat between hot or cold water and seawater, indoor aquaculture tanks maintain optimal breeding conditions.

Conclusion

Space and load capacity are major constraints on offshore platforms. Plate heat exchanger skids, with compact, lightweight, and easy-to-maintain design, significantly contribute to rapid development and operational efficiency in marine engineering projects.

content:
Under the guidance of global carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, supercritical carbon dioxide (S-CO₂) Brayton cycle power generation technology has become a central focus of the energy transition because of its high thermal efficiency, compact system design, and low water consumption. The Printed Circuit Heat Exchanger (PCHE), as the key heat exchange component of this cycle, directly determines the system's performance and commercial value.

This article analyzes the cycle's process flow, explains the limitations of traditional heat exchangers in this application, and demonstrates the core technical advantages of PCHE.

1. Supercritical CO₂ Brayton Cycle Power Generation Core Process

The system uses supercritical CO₂ as the working fluid and achieves efficient conversion of heat to electricity through a closed-loop cycle with no gas-liquid phase change in the traditional sense. The cycle comprises six key stages: the low-temperature, low-pressure working fluid (33 °C, 8.1 MPa) is compressed by a compressor to 20-23 MPa. It then passes sequentially through a low-temperature recuperator and a high-temperature recuperator to recover waste heat and raise its temperature.

Next, it is heated by a heater, using heat sources such as industrial waste heat or solar thermal energy, to 500-800 °C and enters a turbine-generator set to perform work and generate electricity. Finally, it is cooled by a cooler back to its initial state, completing the cycle. Research data shows that when the turbine inlet temperature exceeds 550 °C, the cycle's thermal efficiency is 20%-50% higher than that of a traditional steam Rankine cycle, and water usage is reduced by 50%.

The recuperators and cooler handle more than 90% of the heat exchange duty, making them critical to efficient system operation.

2. Limitations of Traditional Heat Exchangers

Supercritical CO₂ cycle conditions are characterized by high pressure (8-23 MPa, reaching above 30 MPa at the upper end), high temperature (500-800 °C), rapidly changing fluid properties, and small temperature differentials for heat exchange. Traditional heat exchangers struggle to accommodate these conditions. Shell-and-tube heat exchangers require significantly thickened walls under high pressure, and a 50 MW-class recuperator of this type can reach a volume of several hundred cubic meters, over five times that of a PCHE, resulting in a very large footprint.

Plate-fin heat exchangers have brazed seams that are prone to leakage and a maximum pressure tolerance of under 15 MPa, which cannot meet the requirements of medium- and high-pressure systems. In addition, traditional exchangers often have low heat transfer coefficients and large pressure drops, accounting for more than 60% of total system pressure loss. According to estimates, this can lead to a 3-5 percentage point drop in net efficiency for a 10 MW-class system.

Furthermore, with a specific surface area below 500 m²/m³, traditional heat exchangers fail to meet compact system integration needs.

3. Core Technical Advantages of PCHE

PCHEs are fabricated using a combination of chemical etching and vacuum diffusion bonding technologies, together with microchannel design that typically ranges from 0.1-2 mm. This makes them highly suitable for the demanding operating conditions of supercritical CO₂ systems. The core technical advantages include:

Exceptional Pressure and Temperature Resistance

PCHEs can withstand pressures up to 100 MPa and temperatures exceeding 800 °C, ensuring stable and leak-free operation under extreme high-pressure and high-temperature conditions.

Ultra-High Heat Transfer Efficiency

PCHEs offer ultra-high heat transfer efficiency, with heat transfer coefficients ranging from 2000-5000 W/(m²·K), which is 2-4 times that of conventional heat exchangers. Approach temperature differences can be as low as 2-3 K. In megawatt-scale systems, PCHE recuperators can achieve up to 95% effectiveness, resulting in a thermal efficiency improvement of 20%-25%.

Low Pressure Drop and Enhanced Energy Efficiency

The pressure drop across PCHEs is only 1/3-1/2 that of traditional exchangers. For a 10 MW-class system, this results in a 6%-8% reduction in total system pressure losses and an increase of 2-3 percentage points in net power output.

Highly Compact and Lightweight Design

PCHEs feature a specific surface area greater than 2500 m²/m³, which allows their volume to be only 1/4-1/6 that of equivalent shell-and-tube exchangers. Their significantly lower weight also facilitates easier system integration.

Excellent Material Flexibility

PCHEs can be custom-manufactured using stainless steel, nickel-based alloys, and other suitable materials. This ensures reliable performance under rapidly changing fluid properties and compatibility with various working environments.

4. Conclusion

Currently, PCHE products manufactured by Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. have met the needs of supercritical CO₂ Brayton cycle systems for core heat exchange components, including the high-temperature recuperator, low-temperature recuperator, and precooler. These units can adapt to the harsh operating conditions of supercritical CO₂ working fluid, including high pressure, high temperature, and widely varying properties, while delivering excellent heat transfer performance, controllable pressure drop losses, and strong adaptability to changing conditions.

Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. can provide customized solutions to help your project achieve higher thermal efficiency, lower energy consumption, and optimized costs. Choosing PCHE means choosing an efficient, reliable, and low-carbon energy future.

title: How do I know if my heat exchanger is clogged?
excerpt: Heat exchangers are important components in a variety of industrial applications, providing efficient heat transfer between two fluids. Among them, the welded plate heat exchanger stands ou…
author: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
reviewer: Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd.
content:
Heat exchangers are important components in a variety of industrial applications, providing efficient heat transfer between two fluids. Among them, welded plate heat exchangers stand out for compact design and high thermal efficiency. However, like any mechanical system, they can experience problems, including clogging. Knowing how to identify a clogged welded plate heat exchanger is critical for maintaining optimal performance and preventing costly downtime.

Signs of Clogging in Welded Plate Heat Exchangers

  1. Reduced heat transfer efficiency: One of the first indicators of a clogged plate heat exchanger is a significant decrease in heat transfer efficiency. If the outlet temperature of the heating or cooling fluid is not as expected, the flow path inside the plates may be blocked.
  2. Increased pressure drop: A clogged heat exchanger usually causes an increased pressure drop across the unit. If pressure readings are higher than normal, flow may be restricted by debris or fouling inside the plates.
  3. Unusual noises: If a welded plate heat exchanger begins making unusual noises, such as gurgling or knocking, cavitation or fluid turbulence caused by restricted flow may be occurring. This can be a direct result of blockage and should be investigated immediately.
  4. Frequent maintenance intervals: If the heat exchanger requires maintenance more frequently than usual, it may indicate an underlying problem, including clogging. Regular maintenance is important, but increased frequency may show that the system is not operating efficiently.
  5. Visual inspection: If possible, visually inspect the heat exchanger. Although welded plate heat exchangers are not designed for easy disassembly, visible corrosion, scaling, or deposits on the outside may indicate internal problems. If the plates can be accessed, check for visible clogging or buildup.

Preventive Measures

To avoid clogging in welded plate heat exchangers, consider the following preventive measures:

  • Periodic cleaning: Schedule regular cleaning based on the application and handled fluids. This helps remove buildup before it becomes a serious problem.
  • Fluid filtration: Install filters upstream of the heat exchanger to capture debris and particles that may cause clogging. This is especially important in systems where the fluid may contain solids.
  • Monitor operating conditions: Pay close attention to flow rate and temperature. Sudden changes may indicate underlying problems that could lead to clogging.
  • Use appropriate fluids: Ensure that fluids used in the heat exchanger are compatible and free of contaminants. Using the correct fluid can significantly reduce scaling risk.

Conclusion

Early identification of clogged welded plate heat exchangers can save time, money, and resources. By understanding the signs of blockage and taking preventive measures, you can ensure that the heat exchanger operates efficiently and effectively. Regular monitoring and maintenance are key to extending equipment life and maintaining optimal performance. If you suspect that a heat exchanger is clogged, consult a professional to assess the situation and take appropriate action.

1. The Engineering Challenge: Overcoming Traditional Thermal Limits

In modern process industries, specifically refining, chemicals, and power generation, engineers face a critical conflict: the need for higher energy efficiency and lower emissions versus the physical limitations of traditional heat exchangers(HE). Shell-and-Tube Exchangers: Reliable but suffer from low heat transfer efficiency and massive footprints. Gasketed Plate Exchangers (GPHE): Efficient but limited by gasket failures at high pressures (>25 bar) or temperatures (>180°C). Shanghai Heat Transfer Equipment Co., Ltd. (SHPHE) introduces the HT-Bloc Welded Plate HE. This technology eliminates gaskets entirely, combining high efficiency with durability to solve the industry’s “Efficiency vs. Safety” paradox.

  1. Technical Analysis: Why Traditional Designs Fail

To understand the HT-Bloc advantage, it is necessary to analyze the inherent bottlenecks of traditional heat exchangers.

2.1 Shell-and-Tube Limitations

Despite their popularity, Shell-and-Tube designs face systemic inefficiencies: Laminar Sublayer Resistance: Fluid flow requires high velocities (Re > 2300) to break the laminar boundary layer inside tubes. Shell-Side Dead Zones: Baffles create “dead zones” and bypass streams where heat transfer is negligible. Low K-Values: The Overall Heat Transfer Coefficient (K-value) typically ranges from 200–2000 W/m²·K. This requires large surface areas and massive physical footprints to achieve thermal duties.

2.2 Gasketed Plate Limitations

While efficient (K-values up to 7000 W/m²·K), GPHEs are constrained by their sealing mechanism: Material Failure: Rubber gaskets (EPDM, NBR, FKM) degrade rapidly under high heat or aggressive chemicals (e.g., aromatics, solvents). Leakage Risk: Thermal cycling causes gasket fatigue, leading to potentially catastrophic leaks in hazardous applications. 3. The HT-Bloc Solution Against this backdrop, SHPHE’s HT-Bloc Welded Plate HE offers a targeted and comprehensive solution that addresses all the above-mentioned limitations of traditional designs, bridging the gap between tubular robustness and plate efficiency through a revolutionary structural design.

3.1 Core Structure: “Robust Core, Flexible Shell”

  • Fully : Welded Plate Pack: The heat transfer core is laser/plasma welded, forming a gasket-free pressure vessel. It handles temperatures from -50°C to 400°C and pressures from vacuum to

4.0 MPa. Accessible Frame (4-Side Openable): Unlike fully enclosed shell-and-plate units, the HT-Bloc is equipped with four-side removable panels, enabling mechanical cleaning (e.g., high-pressure water jetting) of flow channels — an essential capability for fouling-prone process services.
